newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices rise amid tight Gulf supply.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices rise amid tight Gulf supply.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices extended their gains Thursday despite the faltering futures market as supply remained fairly tight in the Gulf and buyers pumped gas into storage, market sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average gained another three cents to $2.23-2.26 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the mid-to-high $2.20s.
The work on Transco's Texas line will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
Also, Entergy Corp's 936 megawatt River Bend nuclear unit in Louisiana restarted this morning but was still keeping the Gulf supplies tight.
In south Texas, prices also rose three cents to about $2.14-2.15.
In the East, New York city-gate prices were steady to higher again in the high-$2.40s to low-$2.50s.

Temperatures throughout the Northeast are expected to remain slightly below normal through the week before moderating to about one to three degrees above normal early next week, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices also climbed about three cents to about $2.43-2.46 on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are still at least five degrees below normal, prices gained about four cents to $2.05-2.07.
However, normal to above-normal temperatures are expected to return to most of the Midwest by the weekend, which will likely put a lid on prices.
In west Texas, Permian prices jumped another seven cents to an average of $2.07-2.08 as temperatures in the Southwest continued to hover above seasonal norms.
Southern California border prices were up by an equal amount to the low-$2.20s.

Meanwhile, American Gas Association said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 70 bcf and were still 216 bcf, or 29 percent, over year-ago levels. Eastern storage, which gained 40 bcf last week, was 121 bcf, or 39 percent, above 1996 levels. In the West, stocks rose 11 bcf to 199 bcf, which was still 42 bcf behind year-ago levels.
